title: Zesty Smoky Venezuelan Beef Empanadas
description: A kid-friendly Venezuelan dish featuring hot smoked paprika, these empanadas are perfect for a snack or lunch, with a cultured and flaky crust, and can be served on a slate-tile vessel.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large skillet, cook the ground beef over medium-high heat until browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the skillet and cook until the onion is translucent.
Stir in the hot smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper, and cook for 1 minute.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the empanada dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Use a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass to cut out circles of dough.
Place a tablespoon of the beef mixture in the center of each dough circle.
Brush the edges of the dough with the beaten egg and fold the dough in half to form a half-moon shape, pressing the edges together to seal the empanada.
Place the empanadas on a slate-tile vessel or baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving about 1 inch of space between each empanada.
Brush the tops of the empanadas with the melted score fat.
Bake the empanadas for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.
